purpose: Initial untuned TF-IDF versus Item-KNN; no hyperparameter search in this run

item_knn.orientation: Each Linux candidate retains its 100 most similar distinct games from the full fixed input catalog
item_knn.query_scoring: sum retained similarities divided by ALL remaining positive query games, including unsupported ones

tfidf.parameters: Exactly the existing description-tfidf-v1 manifest; no changes
tfidf.profile: Equal-weight mean of L2-normalized positive game vectors, including zero vectors, then cosine
tfidf.zero_text_games: Retain in catalog, queries and targets; never drop users or replace descriptions after tokenization

validation_selection.primary: NDCG@10 on all fixed validation users
validation_selection.this_run: Report both fixed baselines; no tuning, no refit on validation, no dropping unsupported users
validation_selection.diagnostics: Empty/short lists, catalog coverage, unsupported inputs and targets, train candidate-support quartiles; popularity and exact uniform-random controls
validation_selection.support_buckets: Zero train support separately; positive Linux candidate-support quartiles computed only from train, numpy linear quantiles; side=right for ties

test_policy: Run the unchanged baselines once after validation and correctness checks; never tune using frank test metrics
controls: Train-popularity top10 after same exclusions; uniform-random without-replacement exact expectation over remaining Linux candidates. Diagnostic only, never recommendation filling
limitations: frank has per-game review caps and reviewer-selection bias
Fixed historical Linux catalog; not current platform support or latest releases
TF-IDF has 17 textless Linux candidates and limited CJK segmentation
